title: Bounded above acyclic complexes compute a left derived functor
statement: Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian], and assume $\mathcal A$ has enough projectives: every object admits an epimorphism from an object $P$ for which every map $P\to Y$ lifts across every epimorphism $X\to Y$. Every bounded above cochain complex $X$ has a quasi-isomorphism $P\to X$ with $P$ bounded above and each $P^i$ projective; when $X^i=0$ for $i>b$, one can require $P^i=0$ for $i>b$. Let $V:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be additive and right exact (it preserves cokernels and finite direct sums), and suppose its total left derived functor $LV:D(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal B)$ exists, i.e. in Situation 05S8 of [def-pur-saturated-triangulated-localization], with the homotopy category $K(\mathcal A)$, its quasi-isomorphisms and the functor $Q\circ V$, the left derived functor is defined at every object, with canonical comparison $\varepsilon_C:LV(QC)\to Q(V(C))$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For every bounded above complex of projective objects $P$, $\varepsilon_P$ is an isomorphism. Call an object $A$ left $V$-acyclic when $\varepsilon_{A[0]}:LV(A[0])\to V(A)[0]$ is an isomorphism. For every bounded above complex $C$ of left $V$-acyclic objects, $\varepsilon_C$ is an isomorphism. Consequently, if $a:C\to X$ is a quasi-isomorphism with such $C$, the canonical identification of $LV(QX)$ with $Q(V(C))$ is $\varepsilon_C\circ LV(Qa)^{-1}$. These identifications are natural for maps between augmented resolutions: a square $a'f=ha$ gives $Q(V(f))\varepsilon_C LV(Qa)^{-1}=\varepsilon_{C'}LV(Qa')^{-1}LV(Qh)$.

source.place: Tag 0646, lemma-projective-resolutions-exist; Tag 06XN, lemma-find-existence-computes, applied to bounded above projectives; dual of Tag 015E, lemma-leray-acyclicity. The last equality is naturality of the canonical comparison. Defined at every object: Definition Tag 05S9.

proof.text: For $X^i=0$ above $b$, set $P^i=0$ there and descend in $n\le b$. Form $T^n=X^n\times_{Z^{n+1}(X)}Z^{n+1}(P)$ and choose a projective epimorphism $P^n\twoheadrightarrow T^n$. At $n=b$ this pullback is $X^b$, since both next-cycle objects vanish. Its projections define $a^n$ and $d_P^n$; the cycle inclusion gives $d_P^{n+1}d_P^n=0$, and the pullback equation gives $a^{n+1}d_P^n=d_X^na^n$. Recursion is indexed by $b-n\in\mathbf N$; above $b$ the compatible-pair maps are identities of zero. Hence that lemma applies in every degree and makes $a:P\to X$ a quasi-isomorphism. Thus the resolution has projective terms and the prescribed bound.

source.place: Tag 0646, lemma-projective-resolutions-exist (3), explicit dual recursive construction; epimorphic refinements as in Homology Tag 05PK. Only the refinement criterion stated by the cited node is used.

proof.text: A bounded above projective complex $P$ is K-projective by the cited criterion: degree-zero cocycles and boundaries of its Hom complex are chain maps and null-homotopic maps. Apply the denominator lemma with $F=Q\circ V$. Its essential value is $F(P)$ and its identity-stage leg is the identity. By the assumed denominator-diagram definition of $LV$ and its canonical comparison, $\varepsilon_P$ is invertible. This includes projective objects in degree zero and zero.

source.place: Tags 05S8 and 05S9, denominator-diagram definition; dual of the denominator-section argument in lemma-injective-acyclic. The two K-projective facts are the cited Mathlib leaves.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal E$ be the left $V$-acyclic objects. Naturality makes $\mathcal E$ invariant under isomorphisms; Step 2 puts projectives and all zero objects in it. Clause (1) of the short-exact-sequence lemma, applied to $0\to A\to A\oplus B\to B\to0$, gives finite-sum closure. Clause (2) gives kernel closure and short exact image sequences for epimorphisms between members of $\mathcal E$. Its hypotheses are precisely those imposed on $V,LV$ here.

source.place: Dual of Tag 015D, lemma-F-acyclic-ses, clauses (1) and (2).

proof.text: Resolve a bounded above termwise $\mathcal E$ complex $C$ by $a:P\to C$ from Step 1. The cone criterion makes $E=\operatorname{Cone}(a)$ acyclic. Its terms $C^n\oplus P^{n+1}$ belong to $\mathcal E$ by Steps 2--3, and it vanishes above the same bound $b$ as $C$, since $P$ was chosen with that bound. The descending-cycle lemma makes $V(E)$ acyclic. The cone formula and additivity identify $V(E)$ with $\operatorname{Cone}(V(a))$ (the matrix entries are $V(d_C),V(a),0,-V(d_P)$). The cone criterion therefore makes $V(a)$ a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 015E, lemma-leray-acyclicity, dual conclusion; explicit descending-cycle proof from dual Tag 015D. The cone formula is the one in the cited derived-category definition.

proof.text: Naturality at $a$ gives $Q(V(a))\varepsilon_P=\varepsilon_C LV(Qa)$. All factors except $\varepsilon_C$ are invertible by Steps 1, 2 and 4, so $\varepsilon_C=Q(V(a))\varepsilon_P LV(Qa)^{-1}$ is invertible. For any augmented resolution $c:C\to X$ as in the statement, the canonical identification is consequently $\varepsilon_C LV(Qc)^{-1}$, independent of the auxiliary $P$.

source.place: Tag 015E, canonical comparison; formal naturality and inversion in the localized category.

proof.text: For $a'f=ha$, naturality gives $Q(V(f))\varepsilon_C=\varepsilon_{C'}LV(Qf)$ and functoriality gives $LV(Qa')LV(Qf)=LV(Qh)LV(Qa)$. Multiplication by the two augmentation inverses gives $LV(Qf)LV(Qa)^{-1}=LV(Qa')^{-1}LV(Qh)$. Substituting proves exactly the naturality equation in the statement.

source.place: Naturality of the canonical comparison of Tag 05S9; explicit algebra of the displayed square.
